part.text:
All 24 tests pass. I implemented the eight operations in `list_ops.py` recursively, without relying on built-in list helpers, as the spec requires:

- **`append`** — recursively conses each element of the first list in front of the second.
- **`concat`** — flattens one level by appending each sub-list to the concat of the rest (order preserved).
- **`filter`** — keeps elements where the predicate is true, recursing on the tail.
- **`length`** — counts by recursion instead of `len()`.
- **`map`** — applies the function to the head and recurses on the tail.
- **`foldl`** — `function(initial, list[0])` becomes the new accumulator, recursing left-to-right.
- **`foldr`** — `function(foldr(rest, initial), list[0])`, so the accumulator is passed first while elements are applied right-to-left (this ordering was the subtle part, per the spec's note).
- **`reverse`** — `reverse(tail) + [head]`.

`list_ops_test.py` was not modified, and no new files were created.
